To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a nonlinear Landau equation coupled with a heat equation is obtained for describing the nonlinear evolution of disturbances in locally parallel boundary layers, (2) the limit of solutions for large times is calculated and interpreted as a temporallly periodic bifurcation solution in the case of temporal instability, and (3) a non-zero limit of the time-dependent mean flow distortion is found at the outer edge

(i) the mean-flow distortion decaying far from the wall is a solution of an inhomogeneous linear heat equation, which has to be solved in addition to the Landau equation, (ii) the mean-flow deformation at the outer edge is a constant vector that is not necessarily equal to zero, and (iii) a Landau equation with a mean-flow distortion that decays far from wall is equivalent to the Landau equations for a parallel flow with a constant mean deformation at the outer boundary

the mean-flow distortion in a locally parallel boundary-layer flow is not necessarily equal to zero at the outer edge, and that the Landau equation, coupled with a heat equation, describes the nonlinear development of a spatially periodic disturbance in a locally parallel three-dimensional boundary layer.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the assumption of locally parallel boundary layers is not sufficient for the analysis of weakly unstable boundary layers.
the nonlinear development of small disturbances in boundary layers is governed by a system of two nonlinear differential equations for the amplitudes of the disturbances and the mean-flow distortion.
the assumption of local parallelism of boundary layers is not a good one, and that it should be avoided in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonlinear development of a disturbance in a locally parallel boundary-layer flow can be described by a Landau equation.
the Landau equation is a powerful tool for investigating the nonlinear development of boundary-layer disturbances.

the nonlinear development of small disturbances in a locally two- or three-dimensional boundary-layer is described by an amplitude equation for the amplitude of the disturbances and an inhomogeneous mean-flow equation for the mean-flow distortion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mean-flow deformation at the outer edge is an important quantity in the nonlinear development of boundary layers.
a parallel flow is not a good approximation of the flow field in the vicinity of the boundary layer.
the mean-flow distortion, which is caused by the nonlinear disturbance, has to be considered in the linear disturbance differential equation.
